title: Agent Archivist deterministic identifier, object-key, and signature constructions (v1)
description: The byte-exact construction of every derived value in the ingest wire family (plan Sections 7.2, 7.4, and 7.8): the domain-separated identity hashes, the plain canonical payload digest, the server-derived object-key segments, and the Ed25519 signing constructions for ingest attempts, receipts, and the receipt-key certificate. This document is a construction registry, not an instance shape: no instance ever carries these derivations as fields — they are reproducible from the fields named here, which is exactly what makes a lost-response retry converge on the same occurrence, attestation, and keys (STO-004) and what lets a standalone verifier reproduce signatures without importing the protocol crate. Golden vectors over these constructions arrive with the language-neutral conformance corpus; this file pins what they must agree with.

x-archivist.hashOutput: 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters (the derived identifier value on the wire)
x-archivist.labelEncoding: UTF-8 bytes of the domain label followed by one 0x00 byte
x-archivist.fieldEncoding: each field: 8-byte unsigned big-endian byte length followed by exactly that many field bytes

fieldKinds.text: UTF-8 bytes of the canonical wire text of an identifier, enum token, or UUID (identifiers hash as their canonical lowercase text, never as decoded binary)
fieldKinds.u63: 8-byte unsigned big-endian rendering of the non-negative integer
fieldKinds.digest: the 32 raw bytes a 64-character lowercase hex digest names
fieldKinds.bytes: the raw bytes themselves (canonical payload only)

derivations.label: session-v1
derivations.description: Namespaces a logical session by tenant, origin client, harness, and upstream session ID (plan Section 7.4; SID-001). Hostname never enters (mutable provenance); origin-client scope contains cloned harness UUIDs (SID-002).

derivations.label: artifact-v1
derivations.description: Identifies the artifact inside the session namespace, including the adapter and projection version so an adapter change is a different artifact, not a rewrite (plan Section 7.4).
SHA-256 over the canonical uncompressed payload bytes with no domain label (plan Section 7.4). The one digest that names a blob (STO-001); the server recomputes it while streaming (VAL-004).

derivations.label: occurrence-v1
derivations.description: Deterministic occurrence identity (plan Section 7.4; SID-005): session namespace, artifact identity, generation, range, and blob digest. Overlapping, gapped, or re-declared ranges produce distinct occurrences (PI-05); uploader and request never enter, so concurrent authorized uploaders converge on one key (STO-004).

derivations.label: attestation-v1
derivations.description: Deterministic upload-attestation identity (plan Section 7.4; STO-013): the occurrence plus who uploaded it under which frozen request. Retries of one frozen request reproduce it; a distinct authorized uploader or request stays separately auditable.

objectKeys.description: Blob key: pinned storage-profile prefix, digest shard, full digest (plan Section 7.5).
Occurrence key: raw upstream identifiers only ever appear as the hashed session and occurrence values, never as themselves (plan Section 7.5).
Attestation key: occurrence shard, occurrence, attestation (plan Section 7.5).

signatures.key: the linked uploader client key (plan Section 7.2)
signatures.description: The per-attempt Ed25519 HTTP message signature (plan Section 7.2). Each covered value is encoded per fieldEncoding in the pinned order under the ingest-attempt-v1 label; the signature value and its algorithm are not covered (the algorithm is pinned by the closed v1 enum and the linked-key record, whose key ID is covered).

signatures.key: the tenant-scoped server receipt key named by the embedded certificate (plan Section 7.8)
covered: canonical receipt bytes minus the `signature` member
signatures.description: The receipt signature covers the RFC 8785 canonicalization of the receipt object with the `signature` member removed — unknown additive fields are retained inside the signed bytes (plan Section 7.1). The algorithm is pinned by the certificate, so it travels verified rather than trusted.

signatures.key: the tenant authority key the client pinned during linking (plan Sections 7.4 and 7.8; ID-009)
covered: canonical certificate bytes minus the `authority_signature` member
signatures.description: The tenant-authority signature over the receipt-key certificate record with its `authority_signature` member removed (the member name is pinned by the certificate definition in the receipt schema). This is the chain an offline client verifies: pinned authority root signs the certificate, certificate key signs the receipt, and rotation stays non-invalidating because old records verify indefinitely.
